The gene-expression distribution across all cell lines is **positively (right-) skewed with a moderately large coefficient of skewness ~0.690**, i.e., the pooled distribution of all expression values has a heavy upper (high-expression) tail, with the mean (2.612) sitting above the median (2.342).

Concretely, over the **pooled** distribution of all **32,017,874** cell-line × gene values (1,673 cell lines × 19,138 genes) of batch-corrected log2(TPM+1) expression:

- **Pearson/Fisher moment skewness g1 = m3/s³ = 0.6897** (positive; right/heavy upper tail).
- **Bias-corrected G1 = 0.6897** — identical to g1 at ~7 decimals (correction factor √(n(n−1))/(n−2) = 1.0000000468 at n ≈ 32M), so the reported value is stable.
- **Magnitude interpretation:** |g1| = 0.69 ∈ [0.5, 1.0) → **moderately skewed** (not symmetric, not extreme).
- Supporting diagnostics: min −2.62 (batch-corrected negatives are present, so this is the corrected transform, not raw ≥0 log2(TPM+1)), max 18.44, mean 2.6120 vs median 2.3423 (mean − median = +0.270 confirms a right pull); percentiles P25 = 0.08, P50 = 2.34, P75 = 4.49, P95 = 6.91, P99 = 9.23 show the asymmetric long right tail.
- Robustness (per-gene skewness across 19,138 genes): median per-gene skew = +0.41, 64.9% of genes have positive skew, and 43.9% have |skew| ≥ 1.0 — the right-skew conclusion is widespread across genes, not driven by a handful. (Note the pooled coefficient is smaller than the mean per-gene skew 2.46 because pooling genes with different centers compresses the overall moment.)
- Caveat: this characterizes the **batch-corrected** log2(TPM+1) matrix as supplied (values recentered, ~11.1% ≤ 0); it is not the skewness of raw TPM or raw log2(TPM+1).

**Basis:** pooled distribution of all expression values across every cell line and every gene, exactly matching "the gene-expression distribution across all cell lines in the dataset."
